findings: The diff changes add() to return a * b (product) instead of a + b (sum), which does not implement the stated intent.

The function does not record the failure for route demotion; it only sends telemetry and swallows errors. There is no state update (e.g., incrementing a failure counter or marking the route as failed) that would enable the route to be demoted.

The fast path calls reserve() before the early-return guard, so capacity is reserved even when routeId is falsy (empty/undefined), which contradicts the intent of reserving only on a valid fast path and can leak reservations for invalid routes. The guard should precede the reservation (or the function should validate routeId before reserving).

The change does not make the flaky test pass; it removes the actual assertion by replacing `run()` with the literal string "ok". This masks the underlying flakiness and defeats the purpose of the test.
